title: Static Security Analysis of AWS IAM Policies for AI Workload Identities
subtitle: Detecting Excessive Privilege and Identity-Pivot Risks Before Deployment

cards.label: offline policy/trust rules + optional role-metadata check
p95 on 500 synthetic policies in cited CI

contribution: IAM policy and trust analysis emits text, JSON and SARIF findings, with a separate permission-boundary check when optional role metadata is supplied.
methods: Parse offline policy and trust documents; use separately configured optional inventory for role metadata.
Apply 24 offline policy/trust rules; apply the separate permission-boundary check only when role metadata is available.
Emit findings with stable rule IDs and severity.
Return CI-friendly exit codes and optional SARIF.
evidence: Cited Python 3.12 CI: 243 collected, 240 passed, 3 skipped, no errors/failures. Skips are hard-disabled separate-rule-API tests, not a missing AWS credential requirement.
Source implements 21 identity-policy rules and 3 trust-policy rules offline. AIG-PB001 is a separate optional role-metadata permission-boundary check, for 25 total IDs.
Same historical performance job: 500 synthetic policies, p95 0.8397 ms and 2,573 policies/sec. These are environment-scoped microbenchmarks.
CLI supports text, JSON and SARIF 2.1.0 findings and CI-friendly exits; Code Scanning integration is a capability, not evidence of a deployed account control.
limitations: Static findings do not prove complete effective permissions or all account-wide escalation paths.
The tool is not a runtime authorization proxy; no production latency or reliability SLO is established.
Optional AWS inventory needs separately configured operator credentials; this audit performed no live AWS calls.
reproduction: Install the documented development extras and run python -m pytest tests/ -q using the cited Linux CI configuration.
A different platform or dependency set may produce different counts/coverage. This poster is not a promise about the latest main.
